==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈkaʊnt/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-account.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aʊnt|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ac|count}}

===Etymology 1===
{{wikidata lexeme|L4482}}
{{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:acounte|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pewH-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|acounte}}, from {{der|en|xno|acunte||account}}, from {{der|en|fro|aconte}}, from {{m|fro|aconter||to reckon}}, from {{der|en|la|computō||to sum up}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|accounting}} A [[registry]] of [[pecuniary]] [[transaction]]s; a written or printed statement of [[business]] [[dealing]]s or [[debt]]s and [[credit]]s, and also of other things subjected to a reckoning or [[review]]. {{defdate|from c. 1300}}
#: {{ux|en|The firm failed to file its '''accounts''' on time.}}
# {{lb|en|banking}} A [[bank account]]. <!-- Not {{defdate|from 1833}} but 1805 or older: [https://books.google.com/books?id=V7w7AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA961&dq=%22account+at+the+bank%22] -->
#: {{ux|en|The money was refunded to her '''account'''.}}
# A statement in general of reasons, causes, grounds, etc., explanatory of some event; a reason of an action to be done.
#: {{syn|en|accounting|explanation}}
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|date=2012-01
|author=Stephen Ledoux
|title=Behaviorism at 100
|volume=100
|issue=1
|page=60
|magazine=w:American Scientist
|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2012/1/behaviorism-at-100
|passage=Becoming more aware of the progress that scientists have made on behavioral fronts can reduce the risk that other natural scientists will resort to mystical agential '''accounts''' when they exceed the limits of their own disciplinary training.
|accessdate=12 May 2013
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110010832/http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2012/1/behaviorism-at-100
|archivedate=10 November 2013
}}
#: {{ux|en|No satisfactory '''account''' has been given of these phenomena.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|book=Luke|chapter=16|verse=2|passage=Give an '''account''' of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.}}
# A [[reason]], [[ground]]s, [[consideration]], [[motive]]; a person's [[sake]].
#: {{ux|en|Don't trouble yourself on my '''account'''.}}
#: {{co|en|on no '''account'''}}
#: {{co|en|on every '''account'''}}
#: {{co|en|on all '''accounts'''}}
#* {{RQ:Joyce Ulysses|chapter=Episode 16|passage={{...}} who evidently a glutton for work, it struck him, was having a quiet forty winks for all intents and purposes on his own private '''account''' while Dublin slept.}}
# A record of events; a [[relation]] or [[narrative]]. {{defdate|from c. 1610}}
#: {{syn|en|narrative|narration|relation|recital|report|description|explanation}}
#: {{ux|en|An '''account''' of a battle.}}
#* {{RQ:Howell Londinopolis|text=A laudible '''account''' of the city of London.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1920|volume=15|number=2|work={{w|Classical Philology (journal)|Classical Philology}}|title=Hittite an Indo-European Language?|author={{w|Carl Darling Buck|Carl D. Buck}} |page=185|doi=10.1086/360279|passage=The study of the main body of Hittite texts was intrusted{{sic}} to the Austrian scholar {{w|Bedřich Hrozný|Hrozny}}, who in 1915 published a preliminary '''account''' of his results{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1991
|author=Thomas Lawton
|title=A Time of Transition: Two Collectors of Chinese Art
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6kDsAAAAMAAJ
|ISBN=9780913689301
|OCLC=37899659
|OL=8323020M
|page=63
|text=According to one published '''account''', said to be based on information provided by foreign missionaries in Chungking, whose reaction may have been influenced by the excesses of the Boxer Rebellion just a few years earlier, Tuan-fang was killed by his own soldiers at Tzu-chou, Shensi province.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Yunzhong Shu|title=Buglers on the Home Front: The Wartime Practice of the Qiyue School|publisher=State University of New York Press|isbn=0791444376|chapter=2|page={{gbooks|AdkJ8gcb9F0C|58|account}}|passage=In a lapidary style, Qiu Dongping clearly and forcefully describes battlefield actions with simple sentences, giving a blow-by-blow '''account''' of successive events with neither understatement nor exaggeration.}}
# An [[estimate]] or [[estimation]]; [[valuation]]; judgment.
# [[importance|Importance]]; [[worth]]; [[value]]; [[esteem]]; [[judgement]].
#* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|book=XIV|section=footnote|page=235|passage=There is a peculiarity in ''Homer''{{'}}s manner of apoſtrophizing ''Eumæus'', and ſpeaking of him in the ſecond perſon; it is generally apply'd by that Poet only to men of '''account''' and diſtinction, and by it the Poet, as it were, addreſſes them with reſpect; {{...}}}}
# [[authorization|Authorization]] as a specific [[register]]ed user in [[access]]ing a [[system]].
#: {{syn|en|membership|registration}}
#: {{meronyms|en|username}}
#: {{ux|en|Since the system outage, I've been unable to log in to my '''account'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000| title=5,110 Days in Tokyo and Everything's Hunky-dory|author=Sean Mooney | page=66| passage=In these cases, the agency has to buy through another ad agency that has an '''account''' with the media vehicle in question.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[reckoning]]; [[computation]]; [[calculation]]; [[enumeration]]; a record of some reckoning.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide
|passage=It seems that this severity weakened his frame, for three years syne come Martinmas he was taken ill with a fever of the bowels, and after a week's sickness he went to his '''account''', where I trust he is accepted.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[profit|Profit]]; [[advantage]].
#: {{ux|en|The young man soon turned his woodworking skills to some '''account'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=I|passage=I removed from the Old Jewry to Fetter Lane, and from thence to Wapping, hoping to get business among the sailors; but it would not turn to '''account'''.}}

===Etymology 2===
{{wikidata lexeme|L1356}}
{{etymon|en|id=verb|:der|fro:aconter|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|fro|acounter}}, {{m|fro|accomptere}} et al., from {{m|fro|a-}} + {{m|fro|conter||to count}}). Compare {{m|en|count}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To provide explanation.
## {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To present an account of; to [[answer]] for, to [[justify]]. {{defdate|14th|17th c.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|now|_|rare}} To give an account of financial transactions, money received etc. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[estimate]], [[consider]] (something to be as described). {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:deem}}
##: {{ux|en|I'd '''account''' it a privilege to serve you.}}
##* {{RQ:Carlyle Past and Present|III|8|passage=The Pagan Hercules, why was he '''accounted''' a hero?}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[consider]] {{m|en|that}}. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
##* {{RQ:KJV|Hebrews|11|19|text='''Accounting''' that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To give a satisfactory evaluation {{m|en|for}} financial transactions, money received etc. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|An officer must '''account''' with or to the treasurer for money received.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To give a satisfactory evaluation {{m|en|for}} (one's actions, behaviour etc.); to [[answer]] {{m|en|for}}. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|We must '''account''' for the use of our opportunities.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To give a [[satisfactory]] reason {{m|en|for}}; to [[explain]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Idleness '''accounts''' for poverty.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|author=Heather Westwood;Will Mandy;Rebecca Brewer|title=The Relationship Between Interoception, Alexithymia, Autistic Traits and Eating Pathology in Autistic Adults|date=2025-02-14|work=Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10803-024-06708-5|doi=10.1007/s10803-024-06708-5|passage=While the overall model was invariant across groups, the direct relationship between atypical eating (not driven by weight/shape) and ED pathology was only significant in the autistic group. Therefore, while body image appears to contribute to ED pathology in autistic adults, atypical eating may represent an additional unique risk factor for ED pathology. While the correlational nature of this study precludes inferences about causality, the combination of atypical eating and body image dissatisfaction may partially '''account''' for elevated ED pathology in autism.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312190027/https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10803-024-06708-5|archivedate=12 March 2025}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To establish the location {{m|en|for}} someone. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|After the crash, not all passengers were '''accounted''' for.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To cause the [[death]], [[capture]], or [[destruction]] of someone or something (+ {{m|en|for}}). {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Thackeray Vanity Fair|chapter=45|passage=Desperately bold at last, the persecuted animals bolted above-ground—the terrier '''accounted''' for one, the keeper for another; Rawdon, from flurry and excitement, missed his rat, but on the other hand he half-murdered a ferret.}}
# To count.
## {{lb|en|transitive|now|_|rare}} To [[calculate]], [[work out]] (especially with periods of time). {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|edition=2nd|text=neither the motion of the Moon, whereby moneths are computed; nor of the Sun, whereby years are '''accounted''', consisteth of whole numbers, but admits of fractions, and broken parts, as we have already declared concerning the Moon.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[count]] (up), [[enumerate]]. {{defdate|14th|17th c.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[recount]], [[relate]] (a narrative etc.). {{defdate|14th|16th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|III|6|passage=Long worke it were / Here to '''account''' the endlesse progeny / Of all the weeds that bud and blossome there [...].}}
# {{used in phrasal verbs|account for|account of|account to|lang=en}}
